correctness.rationale: In exact arithmetic A<X> is A^(1/2) times the projector onto the whitened sketch span times A^(1/2). On the active two coordinates, a monochromatic sketch of projective sign s has residual (c/2)[[1,-s],[-s,1]], c=2ab/(a+b); both signs give zero residual. A held-out sign t therefore gives centered basic error -cst in the former case and zero in the latter. For m>=3 the all-equal, singleton-minority, and remaining sign families have counts 2, 2m, and 2^m-2m-2; the singleton case has only one nonzero basic error c and gives Q=c^2/m^2. The mean is unbiased; MSE and expected squared diagnostic have ratio m+1. Each basic variance is c^2*2^(2-m), and any pair's covariance c^2*2^(1-m) because both are nonzero only in the all-equal case. At m=2 both errors equal -c*s_1*s_2, so the correlation is one and Q=0. The result is for unnormalized independent Rademacher probes and the mathematical pseudoinverse, not a finite-precision inverse. The supplied standard-library checker check_xnys.py was inspected, not run; independent exact rational sign enumeration at (a,b)=(2,5), m=2 through 8 corroborated the law, ratio and correlation. To replay that panel enumerate the 2^m sign tuples per m, construct A-vv^T/(a+b) for the rank-one residual with v=(a,bs), or use zero for a two-sign sketch; accumulate the joint law and pair moments. Finite enumeration is not the arbitrary-m proof.
